holidays.name: National Chicken Boy Day
holidays.description: A day for a very odd roadside celebrity: a 22-foot fiberglass man with a chicken's head, holding a bucket of fried chicken. Fans of Route 66 kitsch and giant roadside statues can pay tribute by visiting him, sharing photos, or eating fried chicken.
holidays.origin: Chicken Boy started as an advertising mascot for a Los Angeles fried chicken restaurant in the 1960s. When the statue faced demolition, artist Amy Inouye rescued it in 1984. In 2007 she installed it on top of her studio along Route 66, where it became a beloved landmark.
holidays.funFact: Chicken Boy stands about 22 feet tall and looks out over Route 66 from a rooftop in Los Angeles, long after the restaurant he was built to advertise closed.

holidays.name: National No Rhyme Nor Reason Day
holidays.description: A playful tribute to the illogical side of English. People celebrate with nonsense, odd traditions, and trivia about words that famously have no perfect rhyme, such as "orange" and "silver."
holidays.origin: The observance is an unofficial one built around an old idiom. The phrase "neither rhyme nor reason" appears in John Russell's Boke of Nurture from around 1460. Shakespeare later used it in The Comedy of Errors.
holidays.funFact: The idiom is more than 500 years old, and people still argue over whether "orange" has a true rhyme.

holidays.name: Pink Cadillac Day
holidays.description: A salute to one of America's most iconic cars, the pink Cadillac. It's a day for chrome, rock 'n' roll nostalgia, and showing off a bold color choice.
holidays.origin: The day is linked to Elvis Presley's famous 1955 pink Cadillac and to Mary Kay's pink Cadillac rewards program, which began in 1967 and gave top sales performers use of a pink car.
holidays.funFact: Elvis's pink Cadillac became a symbol of his early career and of rock 'n' roll's rebellious spirit.
